ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the attached figure there is a circle, and point A is the center of the circle; the vertical radius from A to point B on the circle is labeled x. The horizontal segment BC through point B is tangent to the circle, and BC is labeled 12. There is also a segment from A going up to the right through the circle and extending to C; the part inside the circle from A to the circle is a radius, labeled x, and the outside part to C is labeled 6, so AC = x + 6. Reasoning: Because BC is a tangent line to the circle, radius AB is perpendicular to tangent line BC, so triangle ABC is a right triangle, with legs AB = x and BC = 12, and hypotenuse AC = x + 6. By the Pythagorean theorem: x^2 + 12^2 = (x + 6)^2. Expanding gives x^2 + 144 = x^2 + 12x + 36, simplifying gives 108 = 12x, so x = 9.

method.method_draft: Read the diagram as a circle with center A, radius AB labeled x, tangent segment BC labeled 12, and a secant/radius line from A through the circle to C where the outside portion from the circle to C is labeled 6; hence AC = x + 6. From the text, use the fact that the segment BC is tangent to the circle. Since a radius to a point of tangency is perpendicular to the tangent, AB ⟂ BC, so triangle ABC is right with legs x and 12 and hypotenuse x+6. Apply the Pythagorean theorem: x^2 + 12^2 = (x+6)^2, then solve to get x = 9.
